correctness.rationale: Computed the map on the matrix units E_ij using the weighted Cauchy dual S'e_j=sqrt((j+2)/(j+1)) e_(j+1) and the positive telescoping projection coefficients. Every matrix diagonal is invariant under the resulting backward bidiagonal operator. The eigenvalue recurrence (lambda-n/(2(n+1)))u_n=(1/2)sqrt((n+2)/(n+1)*(n+d+2)/(n+d+1))u_(n+1) telescopes to u_n=u_0 sqrt((d+1)/((n+1)(n+d+1))) product_(j<=n)(2lambda-1+1/j). For z=2lambda-1 nonzero nonterminating, gamma ratios give |u_n|~const |z|^n n^(Re(1/z)-1). Therefore all |z|<1 occur; |z|>1 do not; on |z|=1 the l2 criterion is Re z<1/2, including z=-1 as a terminating special case. Nonnegative and negative matrix diagonals are orthogonal, and one nonzero eigenvector per diagonal implies infinite geometric multiplicity. No statement about entire spectrum. Independently checked 275 finite exact recurrence identities across d=0..4, five rational z choices and 11 steps, which validate algebra but not the infinite square-summability proof.
